title: Relation preserved under gate remapping
statement: Let $\beta$ be a type, let $f$ assign an output in $\beta$ to each gate and list of previous outputs, let $R$ be a relation on $\beta$, let $d\in\beta$, and let $\sigma:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every gate $g$ and output lists $v,v'$, if $R(v'_{\sigma(a)},v_a)$ holds for every argument index $a$ of $g$ (where an out-of-range list index returns $d$), then $R(f(g\text{ with every argument index }a\text{ replaced by }\sigma(a),v),f(g,v'))$ holds. Let $L,L'\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $init,init'$ be lists of lengths $L,L'$, respectively. Suppose $\sigma(v)<L'$ whenever $v<L$, $\sigma(L+i)=L'+i$ for every $i$, and $R(init'_{\sigma(v)},init_v)$ for every $v<L$, again using $d$ for out-of-range indices. Let $gs$ be a gate list such that, for each position $i$ in $gs$, every argument index of its gate is less than $L+i$. Then for every $v<L+|gs|$, the output at index $\sigma(v)$ from running the remapped gates on $init'$ is related by $R$ to the output at index $v$ from running $gs$ on $init$, with out-of-range indices interpreted as $d$.
